summary: Wired the agent-server to auto-populate the System prompt editor with Pi SDK's actual default system prompt. A new `recordDefaultSystemPrompt` cache in `instruction-files.ts` captures `session.systemPrompt` during session creation when no override is set, and `pi-session-factory.ts` calls it. The editor's `readInstructionFile` returns that cached default when the file is missing, while still treating it as non-existent so Save creates the override file normally.
decisions: Capture the default system prompt by reading `session.systemPrompt` after session construction (instead of replicating Pi's prompt-building logic), because Pi's default depends on cwd, active tools, and skills and isn't exported as a standalone builder.
Return the captured default from `readInstructionFile` only when the file is missing, with `exists: false`, so the UI prefill doesn't suppress the normal 'save creates the override file' behavior.
